Definition: from G5453; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage:--(man-)kind, nature(-al).
BiblicalUsage: Physis is nature — what a thing is by birth and growth. We were by nature children of wrath, says Ephesians 2:3, yet Peter promises we may become partakers of the divine nature in 2 Peter 1:4. Gentiles do by nature the things of the law in Romans 2:14, and Romans 11:24 says God grafted wild branches contrary to nature into His own olive tree.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe my nature was my prison until God gave me a share in His. That grafting — wild into good, contrary to nature — is the whole gospel in one word.
